messages:
maya: quick sync — followup on the KV-cache aware dequant scheduling we discussed. want to lock down the kernel selection and rollout plan for int8/fp8/int4 attention paths.

sanjay: +1. main Q: do we extend the KernelRegistry signature or add a policy layer that picks staged kernels?

liam: leaning towards a small policy layer. keep register_kernel stable, add `selection_policy` hooks. less churn for existing kernels.

elaine: policy layer sounds safer, but we need a clear contract for `dequant_fusion` side effects (peak memory, tmp buffers). if the policy opts-in to fusion, runtime must reserve extra scratch space.

rafa: perf data from local runs: fused int8 attn -> 1.9x tokens/s vs unfused but increases peak by ~14% on A100-40G. fp8 fused is similar but ~6% less stable on long seqs. attached numbers in CI.

build-bot: ci/perf | attn-quant-suite #22 finished
build-bot: throughput: fused-int8=190k toks/s, unfused-int8=98k toks/s, fused-fp8=185k toks/s (seq=2048, batch=1)

maya: good. tradeoff is clear: fusion pays for throughput but higher peak mem. for Dedicated customers we can expose a policy flag `force_fusion` vs `latency_optimized`. for hosted default we should auto-select based on available free mem in node.

liam: implementation sketch: keep kernel registration as-is. add a SelectionPolicy interface:

```
class SelectionPolicy:
  def choose_kernel(op, model_meta, node_capabilities, kv_layout, traces):
    return kernel_handle
```

policy can inspect `kv_layout` (packed vs interleaved) and `node_capabilities` (fp8 hw support, tensorcore generation) and return a fused or unfused kernel.

elaine: the `kv_layout` bit is important. fused dequant requires contiguous kv for single-pass dequant-copy. that means we might need to canonicalize layouts on first request — pay copy cost once. we should document the copy cost in the policy heuristics.

rafa: also watch alignment/stride for int4 quantized rows; our current KV layout pads to 128 bytes. with int4 we should pad to 256 to avoid weird vector loads. that bumps mem again. :grimacing:

maya: noted. decision options: (A) implement policy layer + keep registry untouched, add per-kernel `fusion_hint` metadata; (B) change registry API to accept `capabilities` and do selection inside registry. pros/cons?

sanjay: A gives better separation of concerns and easier A/B testing. B is simpler for kernel authors but couples registry to runtime state. prefer A.

liam: agree with A. plus we can hot-swap policies (canary behavior) via flag in console.

elaine: operational concerns: canary rollout needs metrics: peak_mem, p50/p95 latency, correctness checks (numerical delta vs fp32 baseline). plan to reuse existing quality-eval suite but add long-seq tests (>=4096) and kv-stress.

rafa: note on correctness: fp8 quant->dequant fusion has rare edge cases near softmax tails; add a small stochastic test comparing logits distribution and sample-level perplexity on a held eval set. flagged when drift > 0.5% relative.

maya: good. rollout plan draft:
- implement SelectionPolicy + kernel `fusion_hint` metadata (liam)
- perf harness runs across node types and seq ranges (rafa)
- add memory reservation logic to runtime for fused kernels (elaine)
- console flag and canary gating (sanjay)
- QA/auto-eval checks (maya)

liam: quick registry metadata example:
```
register_kernel(
  name="scaled_dot_attn_v2",
  dtypes=["fp32","int8","fp8"],
  ops=["attn"],
  metadata={"fusion_hint":"kv_single_pass","max_seq":8192}
)
```

maya: keep metadata small and predictable. `fusion_hint` should be enum: NONE | KV_SINGLE_PASS | KV_STAGED_COPY. `max_seq` is advisory.

rafa: I'll surface perf deltas per model family in the perf dashboard and tag risky combos (int4+packed+kvmode=interleaved).

build-bot: perf/ci | attn-quant-suite #23 queued for matrix: [A100-40G, H100-80G] x seq=[512,2048,4096].

elaine: one more thing — telemetry. we need to tag tokens served by fused vs unfused kernels at request level (not per-model) so we can roll back quickly. tiny metadata on spans should be fine.

maya: agreed. action owners: liam proto policy + registry metadata, rafa perf harness, elaine mem + telemetry changes, sanjay console gating, maya QA evals. I'll open a follow-up RFC PR today with these decisions and the canary checklist.

rafa: thanks — will add the perf numbers and int4 padding notes to the RFC draft.

liam: i'll stub the policy interface in the runtime repo and add unit tests for selection logic.

maya: perfect. if no objections, i'll mark this thread summary as the source of truth for the RFC followup. :thumbsup:

sanjay: :+1:

build-bot: link to draft RFC: https://git.redwood/infr/runtime/rfcs/kv-quant-fusion-2024.md
